docs.title: Proposal approval
docs.text: High-value proposals, or ones with aggressive discounts, should not reach the customer without a manager's sign-off. The CRM includes an approval cycle: when a proposal exceeds the rule, it is held until the manager decides.

docs.title: Set the rule
docs.text:
In Settings → Proposal approval:

Field What it does Require manager approval Turns the approval cycle on or off Value limit (TCV) without approval Above this contract value, the proposal needs approval Max line discount without approval Above this discount percentage on a line, it needs approval

Only one condition needs to be exceeded for the proposal to go for approval.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. The salesperson creates the proposal and tries to move it to Sent, Negotiation or Won.
  2. If the proposal exceeds the rule, the CRM does not let it advance: it keeps it in Created and flags it with the Awaiting approval badge.
  3. The proposal shows up in the Pending approvals panel, at the top of the Proposals screen.
  4. The manager clicks Approve or Reject:
    • Approve - the proposal advances to the state the salesperson intended (e.g. Sent) and fires the associated automations.
    • Reject - the manager can write a reason; the salesperson sees it on the proposal and adjusts before resubmitting.

Who approves

Approving and rejecting are manager actions (groups marked as Manager in Settings). Other users see the pending items but cannot decide.

See the reason

Inside the proposal, a notice always shows the approval status: awaiting, rejected (with the reason) or approved.

➡️ Back to Pipeline · Proposals.

docs.title: Create the proposal
docs.text:
Creating a proposal, from client to totals.

Click + Proposal (or an existing card to edit). The modal opens with the proposal header, with no company and no contact selected - the choice is always yours.

Changing the company brings the contact along

If you change the company halfway, the contact follows: with one person at that company it is picked automatically; with several, the field is left blank and the app tells you how many there are; with none, it tells you to create a contact. With several people it does not pick silently - that would be the easiest way to send the proposal to the wrong person.

docs.title: Field by field
docs.text:
Field Notes Number Automatic (PROP-{year}-{no.}), read-only - resets each year. Company (buyer) The company you are selling to - the anchor of the sale. Value, loyalty and discount live here. Search by name or NIPC. (A sale to an individual has no company.) Contact (who you negotiate with) The person at the company you talk to. Choosing the contact auto-fills the company. It is informative: if the person changes company, the sale does not follow them - it stays with the company. Loyalty months Duration of the recurring SaaS commitment; it feeds the total contract value (TCV). Title Name of the proposal (e.g. CRM Licensing). Validity Date up to which the proposal is valid. Status Created / Sent / Negotiation / Won / Lost. It sits at the end of the form and starts empty - on Save, the app warns if it was left unset. Moving to Lost records the loss reason; to Won, the win reason.

Why Status sits at the end, and empty

It used to be at the top with Created as the default. Two consequences: whoever knew the deal was already closed could not set Won right away (choosing a terminal status locks the form - title, company, contact and lines become read-only), and whoever did not know left the default in place without thinking about it.

Status is now the last decision, taken once the proposal is written, and it is a decision - not a value that was already sitting there. The suggestion came from a learner.

VAT uses the company's region and the discount comes from the company's loyalty tier (or the contact's, for an individual) - see Companies & Contacts.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. Proposals → + Proposal.
  2. Choose the Company (the anchor of the sale) and the Contact you negotiate with.
  3. Set the loyalty months (SaaS), the title and the validity.
  4. Add the catalogue lines (each is One-off or Monthly/Annual/recurring).
  5. Save.

docs.title: Customer interest level
docs.text:
Each proposal has an Interest level field - how interested the customer is in this deal, based on their feedback:

Level Colour Unclassified grey (neutral) Cold blue Warm orange Hot red

In the Pipeline, proposals in play (Sent / Negotiation) stop being white and get tinted with the level colour (left bar + subtle background), so you read each deal's "temperature" at a glance. In addition, the Won column gets a green tone and the Lost column a red tone (with a red total), so the terminal states read instantly.

Audit trail

The proposal records who created/changed it and when - visible in the modal footer.

➡️ Next: Lines & catalogue · back to Proposals.

docs.title: Send by email
docs.text: Send the proposal to the client directly from the CRM.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. On the proposal (or in the action bar), click Send by email.
  2. Choose the email template and the recipient (the client's email comes pre-filled).
  3. Subject and, if you wish, CC/BCC.
  4. Confirm the mode (chip at the top: Real send or Simulated).
  5. Send.

Your signature is added automatically at the end.

docs.title: Online proposal (trackable link)
docs.text:
Instead of sending a PDF "blind", the email carries a link to the online proposal. On the proposal, the Online proposal panel shows the link (copy / open) and, more importantly, what happens next:

  • Opens - how many times the client opened it and when it was last opened. You know whether they have seen it.
  • Acceptance - the client sees the proposal nicely in the browser and accepts with one click (types their name and confirms). The CRM marks the proposal as Accepted (who and when); you then close it to Won.

In the pipeline, the proposal gets the Online badge (link published) or Accepted (the client accepted). The link is published automatically on send, or manually via Publish link.

Needs to be online

The online proposal uses the class server (Supabase). It works when you enter through your class; in fully offline mode the link is not published.

Trainees send in simulated mode

Trainees always send in simulated mode (it logs to the history, does not deliver). It is safe to practise.

Trainees send in simulated mode

Trainees always send in simulated mode (it logs to the history, does not deliver). It is safe to practise.

➡️ Next: Loss reason · back to Proposals.

docs.title: Win reason
docs.text: We recorded why deals are lost. The opposite was missing - and the opposite is what you want to repeat.

docs.title: Recording the win
docs.text:
When you change the status to Won, the proposal asks for the win reason, with its own list:

Reason When Price we won on being cheaper Features the solution did what the others did not Relationship / trust they already knew us, or somebody vouched for us Delivery time we could meet the date the customer needed Referral they came through another customer Sole supplier there was no real alternative Response speed we were the first to reply Other you must say which

There is also a free detail field - "only solution with GDPR included".

Choosing Other forces an explanation

If you pick Other, the detail label changes to "What was the reason? *" and the app refuses to save while it is empty. A record that says only Other cannot be read, filtered or counted - it fills the form without saying anything. See the "Other" rule.

docs.title: Where it comes back
docs.text:
• Analytics → Win analysis - the sibling card to Loss analysis, with the same percentage reading. Side by side, they answer the same question from both ends.
  • Account timeline - the Proposal won entry now shows the reason next to the value.
  • Pulso - "why do we win" returns the top reasons.

In charts and in the timeline you see the text you wrote, not the word Other: a hand-written reason stands on its own instead of going into a common bucket.

Why this is worth discussing with the class

Loss analysis teaches a team to avoid mistakes. Only win analysis teaches it to repeat what worked - and those are different things.

Note one more thing: both lists share Price and Features. If price tops both, price is not what is wrong - segmentation is: you are talking to two kinds of customer at once.

➡️ See the opposite in Loss reason · back to Proposals · see Analytics.

docs.title: Lines & catalogue
docs.text: The proposal lines are the items - chosen from the product catalogue (there is no free-text description).

docs.title: Each line
docs.text:
• Item - chosen from the catalogue (grouped by family › subfamily). When you choose, it fills in the description (locked), price and VAT.
  • Quantity.
  • VAT - adjusts to the client's region. If a line has VAT from another region, "Correct to {region}" appears.
  • ➕ adds a line · 🗑️ removes.

docs.title: Totals (automatic)
docs.text:
Subtotal → per-line discount (free) → the company's loyalty discount → VAT (recalculated proportionally) → total.

No catalogue, no lines

Each line points to a product. First create the items in Products.

VAT by region

Mainland 23/13/6 · Madeira 22/12/5 · Azores 16/9/4. The VAT follows the proposal's client region.

➡️ Next: Pipeline (Kanban) · back to Proposals.

docs.title: Export PDF
docs.text:
Preview and save the proposal as PDF.

Generate the A4 document, ready to print or save.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. Open the proposal → action bar.
  2. Preview - see the "sheet" as it will come out.
  3. Download PDF → in the browser's print window, choose Save as PDF.

The document uses the proposal's template (header, logo, quotation, totals, terms, signature) and the client's data. The footer stays fixed at the bottom of each page.

Switch template

Each proposal can use a different template. Try switching and exporting again to compare.

➡️ Next: Send by email · back to Proposals.

docs.title: Loss reason & reopen
docs.text: When a proposal does not move forward, you record why - for later analysis.

docs.title: Recording the loss
docs.text:
When you change the status to Lost (in the modal or by dragging to the Lost column), the app asks for:

  • Reason - Price / Competition / Timing / No budget / No response / Needs changed / Features / Other.
  • Free note (optional).

What it's for

The reasons feed the Loss analysis in Analytics - you see the biggest cause of loss in your base.

docs.title: Reopen
docs.text:
Changed your mind? On a Lost (or Won) proposal, the Reopen button puts it back into Negotiation.

➡️ Back to Proposals · see Analytics.

docs.title: Pipeline (Kanban)
docs.text:
Proposals are organised by status, in columns you can drag.

Created → Sent → Negotiation → Won / Lost

Each proposal is a card; drag between columns to change status.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Dragging a card between columns changes the status (records who and when).
  • Each column shows the total at the bottom.
  • Dropping into Lost prompts for the loss reason.
  • Won/Lost proposals are locked (read-only).
  • High-value proposals may require manager approval before advancing.

docs.title: Reopen
docs.text:
On a closed proposal, Reopen puts it back into Negotiation and unlocks the lines.

List view

Prefer a table? Switch to List at the top of the module - same data, a different read.

➡️ Next: Export PDF · back to Proposals.

docs.title: Getting started - Trainer
docs.text: In just a few minutes you have your class up and running. There are three steps.

docs.title: 1. Receive the class
docs.text:
The class is created by the platform administration, not by you. You receive:

  • your school's address (for example crm.cr0x.org/school);
  • the class code;
  • your username and password;
  • a recovery code.

Open the address, enter the class code and sign in with your credentials.

Keep the recovery code

The recovery code (e.g. A1B2-C3D4-E5F6) is generated only once, when the class is created, and handed to you with the rest of the credentials. It is how you recover your password if you forget it. Keep it somewhere safe - there is no second copy.

You are the Administrator of your class - you and no one else.

docs.title: 2. Add the trainees
docs.text:
Inside the class, go to Settings → Class trainees. You have two ways:

  • Bulk import (Excel/CSV) - download the Template, fill it in and import. It shows you a preview with errors flagged before saving.
  • Individual - fill in the form and click Add to class.

Full details in Manage the class.

docs.title: 3. Share access
docs.text:
Share your space address with the class code with the class:

https://crm.cr0x.org/escola?t=crm-2026

Each trainee opens the link and signs in with their own username and password.

That’s it!

From here on, each trainee works in their own sandbox. When they submit their work, you receive everything in Submission & validation.

docs.title: Getting started - Trainee
docs.text: Welcome! Here are the essentials to get you started.

docs.title: 1. Enter the class
docs.text:
1. Open the link your trainer gave you (it carries your school address and the class code): 
    https://crm.cr0x.org/escola?t=crm-2026
  2. Type your username and your password.
  3. Click Enter.

Don’t have the link?

On your school’s home screen you can type the class code in the dedicated field and click Enter. If the code doesn’t exist, the app warns you.

docs.title: 2. Get to know your space
docs.text:
Each trainee has their own sandbox - a copy of the CRM just for you, with sample data already loaded. You can create, edit and delete freely: it doesn’t affect your classmates.

Navigation is on the left, grouped (Main, Customer service, Marketing & Analysis, Compliance, System).

See what each module does in Working in the CRM.

docs.title: 3. Change your password (recommended)
docs.text:
1. Click your name (bottom-left corner) → opens My profile.
  2. In Current password, type the current one; in New password, the new one.
  3. Save changes.

Forgot your password?

See Recover your password - you can ask the trainer to reset it.

docs.title: 4. Your photo and your signature
docs.text:
In the same place (My profile) you can set a photo and write your email signature, which is added automatically at the end of the emails you send from the CRM.

These two do not live in your sandbox: they travel with your account. Change computer, clear your browsing data, restore a backup or start over - the photo and the signature come back on their own when you sign in.

The photo is personal data, and it lives on the server

It is the only thing of yours that leaves this browser without you sending it. It is tied to your account in this class, nobody sees it in the class list, and it disappears when the account or the class is deleted.

Setting a photo is optional. Without one you get your initials - and everything works exactly the same.

The detail is in the Legal notice.

docs.title: GDPR & Pedagogy
docs.text:
The GDPR module is the core of data protection (data protection). Everything respects the date filter and there is a printable compliance report.

Consents, data subject requests, RoPA and breaches - in a single module.

docs.title: Module areas
docs.text:
• Consents

    Legal basis, purpose and collection channel.

    Open

  • Data subject requests (DSAR)

    Access, rectification, erasure, portability…

    Open

  • RoPA

    Records of Processing Activities.

    Open

  • Data breaches

    Recording and managing incidents.

    Open

  • Data Subject Portal

    The public portal for consents and rights.

    Open

docs.title: What is practised where
docs.text:
Area Where it is practised Analytics e campanhas Dashboard, Analytics, Campaigns, segmentation, funnel, CAC/LTV Data protection and access GDPR (consents, DSAR, RoPA, breaches), users and permissions

Learning tooltips

Throughout the app, the ⓘ icon brings up the definition of the concept (consent, data subject, breach, RoPA…) and the reference to the slide page.

docs.title: Consents
docs.text: Record of each data subject's consent to the processing of their data.

docs.title: Each consent
docs.text:
• Customer/Data subject it relates to.
  • Purpose - marketing, newsletter, relationship management…
  • Legal basis - Consent, Contract, Legitimate interest, Legal obligation…
  • Collection channel and Date.
  • Status - Active / Withdrawn.

Valid consent

It must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous. The data subject can withdraw it at any time.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. GDPR → Consents tab.
  2. + Consent → choose data subject, purpose, legal basis and channel.
  3. Save.
  4. To withdraw, change the status to Withdrawn (or the data subject does so on the Portal).

➡️ Next: Data subject requests · back to GDPR.

docs.title: Data subject requests (DSAR)
docs.text: DSARs (Data Subject Access Requests) are the requests by which a data subject exercises their rights.

docs.title: Rights (request types)
docs.text: Right What it is Access To know what data exists about you Rectification To correct incorrect data Erasure "Right to be forgotten" Portability To receive the data in a reusable format Objection To object to a processing activity Restriction To restrict the processing

docs.title: Each request
docs.text: • Data subject, Type, Date, Deadline (1 month) and Status (Received / In progress / Completed).

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. GDPR → Requests tab.
  2. + Request (or it arrives via the Data Subject Portal).
  3. Handle the request and update the status.

Deadline

You have 1 month to respond. Requests that are overdue or due soon (≤7 days) show up in the Alerts.

docs.title: Answering: two formats, two rights
docs.text:
On a contact's record there are two buttons, and they are not alternatives - they serve different rights:

Button Right Why GDPR report (PDF) Access - art. 15 The data subject is entitled to a copy of their data and to information in clear language (art. 12(1)). A PDF is the natural format Export JSON Portability - art. 20 The law requires a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format. A PDF does not meet that requirement

docs.title: What the GDPR report includes
docs.text:
Listing the data is not enough. The document also carries what article 15(1) requires:

  • the purposes and legal basis (a), the categories of data (b) and the recipients (c);
  • the retention period (d) and the source of the data (g);
  • the rights to rectification, erasure, restriction and objection (e) and the right to lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority (f);
  • the existence of automated decision-making and profiling (h) - in the CRM, the lead score;
  • identification of the controller and the DPO.

docs.title: Best practice before handing it over
docs.text:
• Verify the identity of the requester (art. 12(6)) - answering the wrong person is itself a data breach.
  • One month to reply, extendable by two more in complex cases (art. 12(3)).
  • First copy is free (art. 15(3)).
  • Minimise: only that person's data - never third-party data that shows up in the same notes.
  • Secure channel for delivery and record the response (accountability, art. 5(2)). When you generate the report, if an Access request is open the CRM offers to mark it as completed.

Careful with internal notes

Notes the team writes in the CRM (e.g. "difficult customer") are personal data and appear in an access request. Good rule: only write what you would be willing to show the person.

➡️ Next: RoPA · back to GDPR.

docs.title: Data Subject Portal
docs.text: A public page where any data subject can review their consents and exercise their rights - without entering the app.

docs.title: What it is for
docs.text:
• The data subject sees the consents they have given.
  • Withdraws a consent.
  • Submits a request (access, erasure, portability…) that goes straight into the Requests (DSAR).

docs.title: How to access it
docs.text:
It opens at #portal (the Data Subject Portal link in the menu/footer). It is public: designed to be shared with customers.

Link to the module

Everything that comes in through the portal appears in the trainer's GDPR module - it is the full circuit of exercising rights, from the data subject to whoever processes the data.

➡️ Back to GDPR.

docs.title: RoPA - Records of Processing Activities
docs.text: The RoPA (Records of Processing Activities, Article 30 of the GDPR) lists what the organisation does with personal data.

docs.title: Each activity
docs.text:
• Name of the activity (e.g. Customer management, Newsletter).
  • Purpose and Legal basis.
  • Categories of data subjects and of data.
  • Recipients and any transfers.
  • Retention period.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. GDPR → RoPA tab.
  2. + Activity → fill in the fields.
  3. Save - it enters the compliance report.

Why it is mandatory

The RoPA is the map of data processing. It is the first document a supervisory authority asks for in an audit.

➡️ Next: Data breaches · back to GDPR.

docs.title: Data breaches
docs.text: Record of security incidents that affect personal data (loss, unauthorised access, leak…).

docs.title: Each breach
docs.text:
• Date and Description of the incident.
  • Affected data and number of data subjects.
  • Severity and measures taken.
  • Notified to the CNPD? and to the data subjects?

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. GDPR → Breaches tab.
  2. + Breach → describe the incident and the affected data.
  3. Record the measures and the notification status.

The 72-hour deadline

A risk breach must be notified to the CNPD within 72 hours. If there is a high risk, the data subjects must also be informed.

docs.title: Guided tutorial: set up the class in 10 minutes
docs.text:
In this tutorial

Goal: enter the class, import the trainees, share access and be ready to receive submissions. · Duration: ~10 min · For: Trainer.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [x] You have your school address, the class code and your credentials.
  • [x] You have the list of trainees (first name, surname, email).

docs.title: Step 1 · Enter the class
docs.text:
1. Open your school's address (e.g. crm.cr0x.org/school).
  2. Enter the class code you were given and sign in with your username and password.

Save the recovery code

It was handed to you with the credentials and there is no second copy. It is your way to recover the password.

Entering the class from your school's home screen.

docs.title: Step 2 · Prepare the list (Excel)
docs.text:
1. Settings → Class trainees → Excel/CSV Template.
  2. Fill in one row per trainee: first name · surname · email · username · password.

Password

If you leave the password column empty, the initial password is used (field on the page) - the same for everyone; each trainee changes it later.

docs.title: Step 3 · Import with preview
docs.text:
1. Click Import list and choose the file.
  2. Check the preview: OK rows in green, errors flagged in red.
  3. Import N valid.

Result

The trainees appear in the list, ready to enter.

Preview

Before saving, you see a table with each row marked ✓ valid or in red (missing field, invalid or duplicate email). Only the valid rows are imported.

docs.title: Step 4 · Share access
docs.text:
Send the class your space address with the class code:

https://crm.cr0x.org/escola?t=crm-2026

Each trainee enters with their own username and password.

docs.title: Step 5 · (Optional) Enable real email sending
docs.text: In Settings → Real email sending, turn on Enable real sending and run Send test. (The keys are fixed; you only manage the mode.)

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• When the trainees hand in, you go to Submission & validation - review, generate PDF, download.
  • Customize the Brand if you want the CRM with a different identity.

docs.title: 2.1 From zero to your first proposal
Guided tutorial: from zero to your first proposal
docs.text:
In this tutorial

Goal: create a company, a contact and an item, build a proposal, export the PDF and submit it. · Duration: ~12 min · For: Trainee (and anyone getting to know the CRM).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [x] You are inside your class (you entered through the ?t=… link).
  • [x] You see the sidebar on the left (Dashboard, Companies, Contacts…).

If you haven’t entered yet, see Getting started - Trainee.

docs.title: Step 1 · Create the company
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, click Companies.
  2. Click + Company.
  3. Fill in Name (e.g. Hotel Sol & Mar, Lda.) and the NIPC (the app validates it).
  4. Choose the Region (e.g. Madeira) - it will set the VAT further on.
  5. Save.

Result

The company appears in the list. Click it to see the 360° view (no contacts yet for now).

📷 Screenshot

docs.title: Step 2 · Create the contact
docs.text:
1. Click Contacts → + Contact.
  2. First name and Surname (e.g. Ana Costa).
  3. In Company, choose the one you created; fill in the Role.
  4. Email, NIF (validated) and the Segment (e.g. SME).
  5. Confirm the Region (it inherits the VAT logic). Save.

Loyalty

The loyalty level (Bronze/Silver/Gold) belongs to the company - it adjusts with the company's purchase volume and the contact inherits it, giving an automatic discount on proposals.

docs.title: Step 3 · Create the item (catalog)
docs.text:
1. Click Products.
  2. + Family (e.g. Software) → + Subfamily (e.g. Licenses).
  3. + Item: name (CRM Pro License), family/subfamily, price (e.g. €79) and VAT. Save.

Why the catalog first?

In proposals, the lines are chosen from the catalog - it ensures consistent prices and VAT.

docs.title: Step 4 · Build the proposal
docs.text:
1. Click Proposals → + Proposal.
  2. Company and Contact: choose the company (the anchor of the sale) and the contact Ana Costa - the region's VAT and the company's loyalty discount now apply. Set the loyalty months (SaaS).
  3. Title: CRM licensing proposal.
  4. Line: choose the item CRM Pro License → description/price/VAT fill in; set Quantity 5.
  5. Note the Totals block (subtotal, discount, VAT, total).
  6. Save.

VAT notice

If the customer’s region doesn’t match the line’s VAT, “Correct to {region}” appears - click it to align.

📷 Screenshot

docs.title: Step 5 · Export the PDF
docs.text:
1. Open the proposal → action bar → Preview (see the A4 sheet).
  2. Download PDF → in the print dialog, choose Save as PDF.

Document look

The layout comes from the Proposal Template. Try switching templates and exporting again.

docs.title: Step 6 · Move through the pipeline and submit
docs.text:
1. In Proposals (Kanban view), drag the card to Negotiation and then Won.
  2. Set your signature in your profile (bottom-left corner) - it is required to hand in.
  3. Click Submit my work → confirm and Submit.

You completed the flow!

You created data, a proposal, a PDF and made the submission - the full cycle of a CRM. 🎉
